text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures climbed further in late trade to highs for the day, relief on Bundesbank/Bonn gold deal supports the market. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.47, up 0/70 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures gained the best part of a point, buoyed by a Bund rally and secure in the knowledge that Britain remains on the sidelines of EMU confusion. News that Germany has backed off its plan to revalue gold reserves boosted the markets. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-14/32, up 25/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Renewed confidence the Socialist victory in Sunday's French poll will not critically harm the move to a single European currency and an end to the German row about revaluing gold reserves trimmed French bond yields. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.40, up 0.88 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to firmer levels near the day's highs in late afternoon dealing after the German government backed down over its controversial plan to revaluate the Bundesbank's gold reserves. But market uncertainty still remains as investors await further developments on EMU. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.85, up 0.67 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries rebound from lows, edge higher in late morning, traders cite buying on dips as September bond bounces off 109-20 support level, and setting up of shorts ahead of jobs data, with the market also watching pricing of numerous corporate issues. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-09/32, up 04/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.89 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended lower on technical selling ahead of a shift forward in benchmark status from the June to the September. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 123.83, up 0.03 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Six sovereign bond offerings featured in the primary market amid a deluge of sizeable new issues. Players were taking advantage of a benign U.S. Treasury market and the usually quiet run-up to the key U.S. employment report, due Friday. Emerging nations led the early charge with Romania and Turkey launching expected mark bonds while Brazil set its well-flagged lira offering.
